input.rationale: Section 1.4 is the operative licence-type grant in our favour (access to and the right to use HDI's system, software and Content administration tools). It runs to "the Company" only — the defined Company is The Deerskin Companies, Inc. alone, with no affiliate coverage and no mechanic to add affiliates — so the grant fails the fallback element requiring affiliate coverage on written notice. Nothing makes the grant revocable or suspendable at HDI's discretion, and Section 10.3 ("shall inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by, the parties hereto and their respective legal representatives, successors and assigns") already permits transfer to a successor in an M&A transaction, so that fallback element is met. We therefore target the fallback level with a single sentence extending the Section 1.4 grant to our affiliates on written notice; contractor coverage and perpetual/irrevocable wording are preferred-level only and not added. The reciprocal licence of our Marks to HDI (Section 6.1) is non-exclusive and non-transferable and needs no change.

mappings.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.

ops.text: The access and rights to use granted to the Company under this Section 1.4 shall extend to the Company's affiliates upon written notice to HDI.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the Section 1.4 access and use rights to our affiliates upon written notice to HDI, consistent with our fallback licence-scope position; the Agreement's successors-and-assigns clause already permits transfer to a successor.
proposal.summary: Extend the Section 1.4 access/use grant to the Company's affiliates on written notice to HDI.
